items.description: The method's write is surgical: comments, key order and every key it was not given survive; a YAML path the values file does not already hold is an error rather than a silently created key; and a run whose tags are unchanged commits and pushes nothing, saying so.
items.rationale: Surgical, and fails loudly where it must. S1's diff is exactly the seven pin lines per file (`":523"` -> `":524"`, the two whole references `...:523` -> `...:524`) and nothing else, so every comment, blank line, key order and unrelated key is byte-identical, and the lines' own double-quoting is kept. S3: a path the file does not hold (`images.nonexistent`) throws `holds no images.nonexistent; a path the file does not already carry is never created` and the remote does not move. S4: a values file the repo lacks throws. S6: the same file named by a String key and a GString key throws `pins names config/dev/values.yaml twice` before any clone. S2: re-running identical pins returns null, the log says `already carries these pins: nothing committed, nothing pushed.`, and the remote does not move. Known limits, already in the close-out and outside this criterion's text: a bare `524`/`true`/`null` written onto a PLAIN-style line reads back as int/bool/None (B2; S10 reproduced it, and the docstring that promised otherwise is narrowed in 2c43b06), and a duplicate path inside one file's pins map is silently last-wins (B3). Neither is reachable from the call shape slices 011/012 use: the five tag suffixes are `:<n>`/`:prd-<n>` on already double-quoted lines, and the two whole references are non-numeric strings YAML never re-types.

items.description: "The committed default tag is a real <n>, never latest (D37)" — strengthened by D47 to no default at all and by Ruling 6 to a chart that refuses to render: with a stage values file missing any one of the seven, helm template fails with a message naming the key. Removing the default alone does not do that — an absent concatenated suffix renders an untagged reference and helm exits 0, and an absent controllerConfig.images key drops silently out of the controller's ConfigMap — so the guard is in the chart, where it protects a hand-edited stage file at sync time, with the gate checking the same property from outside.
items.rationale: Proven on the chart itself, with the gate out of the loop: in a scratch copy of KubeCoderDeploy, deleting each of the seven pins from each stage file in turn (7 x 2 = 14 runs) makes `helm template` exit 1 with a message naming the exact key (`images.<key> is not set: config/<stage>/values.yaml carries Build-Main's seven pins (D47)` / `controllerConfig.images.<key> is not set: ...`). 14/14 refused and named. The five concatenated tags are guarded per container and worker/vsix by a range-guard in controller-config.yaml, which is what closes the toYaml no-per-key-site hole; the guard sits in the chart, so it protects a hand-edited stage file at sync time when `kc project test` does not run.
